description: For ten years, Zeus and the Olympians fight Cronus and the Titans. Their victory founds the order of the Greek world.

hero.hook: Ten years of cosmic war: the children overthrow their fathers to found Olympus.

blocks.text: The **Titanomachy** is the first war of Greek mythology. For **ten years** it pits the **Titans**, the older generation of gods, against the **Olympians** led by the young **Zeus**.
It is not only a family quarrel. It is the move from a world of brute force to a world of order and law. Zeus's victory settles forever who rules the sky, the sea and the dead.

It all begins with **Cronus**, the youngest of the Titans. Having dethroned his own father Uranus, he fears the same fate. He swallows his children as soon as they are born. His wife **Rhea** saves the last one, **Zeus**, by handing over a stone wrapped in swaddling clothes. The child grows up in secret on Crete.

blocks.caption: Titans against Olympians: ten years to decide who rules

blocks.text: In some versions Zeus is fed by the goat **Amalthea**. While playing, he breaks off one of her horns, and it becomes the **horn of plenty**, always full of food.

As an adult, Zeus forces Cronus to bring back up **Hestia**, **Demeter**, **Hera**, **Hades** and **Poseidon**. The young gods settle on **Olympus**. Cronus and the Titans hold Mount **Othrys**, in Thessaly. The war bogs down. More allies are needed.

Zeus frees the **Cyclopes** and the **Hecatoncheires** from **Tartarus**, the prison below the underworld. The Cyclopes, one-eyed smiths, forge the decisive weapons: the **thunderbolt** for Zeus, the **trident** for Poseidon, a helmet of invisibility for Hades.

blocks.caption: The Cyclopes forge the thunderbolt of Zeus

blocks.text: The three Hecatoncheires, Cottus, Briareus and Gyges, have a hundred arms and fifty heads. They tear off whole sides of mountains and hurl them at the Titans. Under the lightning and the rocks, the old world falls apart. The defeated Titans are chained in Tartarus, guarded by the Hecatoncheires, prisoners themselves the day before.

sections.title: Thunderbolt, trident and a hundred arms

blocks.text: The winners draw lots. **Zeus** gets the sky and the command. **Poseidon** gets the sea. **Hades** gets the underworld. The Olympian order replaces the cycle of fathers killed by their sons.

blocks.caption: Zeus, Poseidon and Hades: three brothers, three realms

blocks.text: Some Titans are spared and keep a place in the new order. [[Themis]], who guarantees divine law, stays at the side of Zeus.

The peace stays fragile. **Gaia**, mother of the Titans, gives birth to more threats: the monster [[Typhon]], then the [[Gigantomachy]], the war against the Giants. This time the gods need a mortal, **Heracles**, to win. The age of heroes has begun.

sections.title: Sharing out the sky, the sea and the dead

blocks.text: The word “titanic” still recalls their strength. In 1795 the chemist [[Martin Heinrich Klaproth]] named **titanium** after them, for its toughness. The moons of Saturn, the planet of Cronus for the Romans, carry the names of Titans.

The Titan **Atlas** is remembered for a single image: [[Atlas holding up the sky]] on his shoulders forever. Mapmakers borrowed the figure: [[Mercator]] put his image on collections of maps. Soon the book itself was called an **atlas**.
The Olympians overthrow **Cronus** thanks to the Cyclopes and the Hecatoncheires. The Titans fall into Tartarus. Zeus, Poseidon and Hades share out the world, and the order of Olympus is born.
